final_answer:
MEMORANDUM (privileged work product; not for client until partner review). To: R. Sutherland. From: J. Kravitz. Re: CPS/Ridgeway - Brinkerhoff (Mar. 14) v. FTC Staff (Apr. 2) market-share discrepancies. Draft for Apr. 18.

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) Two FTC markets trigger the 2023 Merger Guidelines presumption: Market 3 (rigid, 8-state) robustly; Market 4 (food-grade corrugated) on stated numbers, but its HHI cannot be reproduced and sits closer to the line than staff says. (b) Brinkerhoff's own Market C (32.9% share, delta 537) triggers the Guidelines' separate >30%-share/delta>100 presumption even on his 12-state definition; his report applies superseded 1,500/2,500 thresholds and says no presumption exists. That is the single worst cross-examination point. (c) The report has real errors (Market C sums, tolling overattribution, six-versus-four peripheral states, Market A fringe HHI, thresholds). (d) The FTC also has soft spots (mixed pricing/time bases, implausible fringe HHIs, unsupported identical shares). (e) A supplemental/rebuttal Brinkerhoff declaration is needed; target filing by mid-May (confirm against the scheduling order, which I have not seen).
Guidelines/case citations are from memory; I could not retrieve the Guidelines text online (egress blocked) and they must be cite-checked.

2. LEGAL FRAME
2023 Merger Guidelines, Guideline 1 (as I recall; verify): presumption if post-merger HHI >1,800 and delta >100, or merged share >30% and delta >100. Presumption is burden-shifting: United States v. Philadelphia Nat'l Bank, 374 U.S. 321, 363-64 (1963); United States v. Baker Hughes, 908 F.2d 981, 982-83 (D.C. Cir. 1990); FTC v. H.J. Heinz Co., 246 F.3d 708, 715 (D.C. Cir. 2001) (rebuttal burden rises with concentration). Submarkets turn on practical indicia: Brown Shoe Co. v. United States, 370 U.S. 294, 325 (1962).

3. CHART (HHI pre / post / delta)
FTC 1 Corrugated: 1,343 / 1,452 / 109. No presumption (HHI<1,800; 20.2%<30%).
FTC 2 Folding cartons: ~1,066 / ~1,202 / 136. No (21.0%).
FTC 3 Rigid, 8-state: 1,396 / 2,194 / 798. YES, both prongs (40.0%). Robust: even with zero fringe HHI, post = 1,216+798 = 2,014.
FTC 4 Food-grade: 1,850 / 2,210 / 360. YES on HHI prong as stated; 29.0% is below 30%.
Brink A Corrugated: 1,184 / 1,268 / 84. No.
Brink B Folding cartons: 958 / 1,066 / 108. No (delta >100 but HHI <1,800; 21.0%).
Brink C Rigid, 12-state: 1,050 / 1,587 / 537. HHI prong no; share prong YES (32.9% >30%, delta >100). The report's conclusion is wrong under the 2023 framework.
Headroom: Market 3 is far above (post 2,194 v. 1,800; 40% v. 30%) so knocking out geography is the only path. Market 4 is nearer the line (below).

4. FOOD-GRADE CORRUGATED (MARKET 4)
Findings. Report omits it as a market; contrary to the partner's note it is not wholly silent: para. 43 rejects end-use sub-markets on supply-side substitution (a box plant serving food can serve electronics) but never mentions FDA 21 CFR 174-178, certification, or the 8-15% premium. Para. 43 is thin and unsupported by data.
Do the numbers clear the thresholds? As stated, yes (2,210; delta 360). But FTC App. D gets pre-HHI 1,850 from named firms 1,401 plus "all others" 449 for a 27.0% fringe. That is mathematically implausible: a fringe whose firms are each below Great Lakes' 6% contributes at most about 160, and even if each were Atlas-sized 10%, at most about 250. Named-only post-merger HHI is 1,761 (<1,800); the HHI prong holds only if the fringe contributes at least 39 points (realistic, e.g., about 5-10 firms gives roughly 70-150). Post-merger is therefore roughly 1,830-1,920, not 2,210: presumption likely survives but the margin is thin and the share prong (29.0%) is missed by 1 point.
Credible challenge to the market: (i) hypothetical monopolist/supply-side: Brinkerhoff para. 43 plus our own facts (same plants, modest changeover); (ii) CPS data show food-grade is 37.8% of CPS finished corrugated ($1,880M of $4,980M), sold to major customers, so food-grade producers are many and customers (Monarch, Great Plains Dairy) multi-source. Risks: CPS's own ledger tracks food-grade as a separate sub-segment; CPS runs FDA-compliance at Henderson; Ridgeway's 9.0% (versus 3.2% overall) shows specialization; Brown Shoe practical indicia (industry recognition, distinct customers, specialized vendors) favor staff; silence invites a concession finding.
Supplemental report: yes. Timeline: engage Trident by Apr. 25; draft May 9; file by mid-May (confirm order deadline). Scope: HMT/SSNIP on food-grade, supply-side substitution (cost/time of certification, which competitors can switch; Sterling's absence per FTC), market shares and HHI with disclosed fringe, entry, efficiencies and customer testimony in food-grade. 

5. DISCREPANCIES BY MARKET (root cause; D = defensible, V = vulnerability)
MARKET A v. 1 (corrugated). Totals $38.6B v. $32.1B; combined 17.8% v. 20.2%; delta 84 v. 109; pre-HHI 1,184 v. 1,343.
- Root cause 1, definition: $6.5B sheet-feeder sales (Brinkerhoff para. 21; FTC II.B). 38.6-6.5 = 32.1 ties. CPS's sheet sales are $810M (14% of its corrugated), so exclusion lifts CPS's share. His supply-side logic (para. 31) is arguable, but counting sheets and the boxes later made from them double-counts the same output; the HMT is applied to finished containers; FTC's end-customer framing is likely more persuasive.
- Root cause 2, pricing: FOB (his) v. delivered (FTC; 3-8% freight). Both bases are inconsistently applied by FTC: its $32.1B equals his FOB $38.6B minus $6.5B exactly, so no freight uplift appears, while its named-firm shares for Atlas, Great Lakes and Sterling (13/9/7) are identical to his despite different totals, implying the same proportional adjustment (Atlas's revenue falls $0.84B, 16.8%, exactly the market ratio). That suggests FTC derived, not independently measured, those figures.
- Root cause 3, period: CPS FY (Oct 2022-Sep 2023) v. CY2023. Lakewood $47M (signed Oct 2023) is outside his period; effect is about 0.15 point of share (47/32,100), trivial. CPS's bridge is itself flawed: line-item "CY2023" columns add Q4 CY2023 to a full FY (15 months; e.g., corrugated $7,325M); only the grand-total note corrects it (6,820-1,650+1,930 = $7,100M, +4.1%). Line-item Q4 increments sum to $2,465M, not $1,930M. A proper CY figure for finished corrugated is roughly $4,980M x 1.041 = $5,185M; x about 5% freight approximates FTC's $5,460M, which likely reconciles FTC's CPS figure.
- Error V: pre-HHI 1,184 requires a fringe contribution of about 168 for a 31.2% fringe the report calls numerous regional producers (equal-split of 25 firms gives about 1,055). The fringe assumption is undisclosed (paras. 57; Exh. E). FTC's Market 1 uses an almost identical fringe contribution (168.76 for "about 34 firms" at 26.7%; equal split about 21), so this is not one-sided, but we must disclose. Delta (84) is unaffected. Report also calls 1,184 "moderately concentrated... below 1,500" (para. 60), and uses the 2010 thresholds (paras. 56, 60, 67).
MARKET B v. 2 (folding cartons). Same definition and $14.2B; combined 21.0% both; delta 108 v. 136.
- Root cause: Brentwood tolling attribution (manufacturer v. seller of record). FTC's position is stronger: Ridgeway invoices, holds the customer, bears credit risk, title passes FOB Henderson, and CPS's non-solicit concedes the account (tolling memo IV.C-G); government data attribute to the invoicing entity.
- Error V (important): Brinkerhoff attributes the full $140M to CPS though CPS makes only about 60% (about $84M, tolling memo IV.B); Ridgeway makes $56M itself. His own report says 60%. Correct 60/40 attribution gives CPS about $2.49-2.50B (about 17.6%) and Ridgeway about $0.49B (about 3.4%), delta about 120, a third set neither side has. CPS's ledger records $140M tolling revenue, while the memo says CPS invoices about $84M; conflict unresolved; pull invoices. Double-count risk: if CPS's $2,410M/$2,420M includes the $84M tolling fee while Ridgeway's $570M includes the full $140M, the FTC doubles it.
- $10M residual: CPS direct sales $2,420M (FY, FOB) v. FTC $2,410M is not a trivial rounding. A CY adjustment (+4.1%) and delivered pricing would push FTC's figure to roughly $2.6B, so the match suggests staff used FY/FOB or offsetting errors hide a larger gap. Likewise FTC's CPS figures for Market 3 ($760M) and 4 ($1,880M) equal CPS's FY FOB ledger exactly, contrary to staff's stated CY delivered method. Also FTC pre-HHI 1,066 (fringe 236 for 40% in sub-10% firms) is above ours despite lower named-firm HHI (830 v. 858); it equals Brinkerhoff's post-merger 1,066, possible copying; with his fringe it would be about 930.
- No presumption on either; delta above 100 on both (108/136); Brinkerhoff's para. 62 calls 108 "slightly above" a screen.
MARKET C v. 3 (rigid containers). Totals $4.8B v. $3.6B; combined 32.9% v. 40.0%; HHI post 1,587 v. 2,194; delta 537 v. 798.
- Root cause: geography. IA, MO, WV, TN add $1.2B but only $140M of party sales (CPS $100M, Ridgeway $40M), so the parties' share falls 7.1 points. Third-party revenue in the four states is about $1.06B, so competitors in them are strong; whether they discipline price in core states is the question.
- Strength/weakness. FTC evidence: 87.3% of shipments into the 8 states originate inside (App. C), customer testimony, 300-mile freight limit, and $15-50M plant capital. Our evidence: report says 300-500 miles; bids from TN/KY/WV; HMT argument; 12.7% inflow. Weaknesses: para. 41 says six core and "six peripheral" states while naming four peripheral (IA, MO, WV, TN), and para. 41 treats KY/WV/TN as bidders while para. 77 lists four; para. 77 argues the parties' small presence in these states proves they are competitive alternatives, which cuts against us; Parties' state split also differs: CPS ledger IA 30/MO 35/WV 15/TN 20 versus FTC App. C 25/30/20/25 (both total $100M); resolve.
- Error V: Exhibit 3 shares sum to 99.7% and revenues to $4.78B versus $4.80B; plus the "undisclosed" fringe (HHI 1,050). This is the most consequential discrepancy. Even if 12 states survive, the 30%-share prong applies, so rebut with entry/expansion (78% utilization claim para. 78, uncited), efficiencies ($85-110M), and customer evidence.
MARKET 4: see section 4.

6. CROSS-EXAMINATION RISK, PRIORITIZED (Nakamura)
1. Market C: expert says no presumption (wrong test; 32.9%). 2. Market 4 silence. 3. Superseded thresholds. 4. Tolling overattribution ($140M v. 60%). 5. Market C arithmetic and six/four state inconsistency. 6. Undisclosed fringe in HHIs. 7. FY/FOB mismatch and unreconciled CPS data. 8. CV: report says fourteen prior testimonies, but Exh. A items 13-14 are FTC staff roles (verify).

7. DATA INTEGRITY RED FLAGS (resolve before any filing)
- CPS segment totals ($5,790+2,560+860+390 = $9,600M) exceed reported $6,820M revenue by $2,780M; ledger deducts only "-780" and explains it unconvincingly (it would not reconcile even then: 9,600-780 = 8,820). Ridgeway's segment revenues (about $1.08B+0.43B+0.72B = $2.23B; FTC $2.28B) exceed its $1.23B total. Segment revenue figures may be double counted or on non-comparable bases; staff has subpoena data and will see it.
- Junior spreadsheet is not reliable: it says the report gives no Market C HHI (it does: 1,050/1,587/537); treats Atlas as having no sheet sales (non-issue) though Atlas's revenue falls $0.84B; did not test FTC's fringe HHIs; and omits the 30% prong and 12-state share presumption. Neither side's pre-HHI could be independently reproduced; all flagged.

8. ADDITIONAL ITEMS
- Pricing (delivered v. FOB): matters. Freight 3-8% shifts firms non-uniformly and changes totals; neither basis is applied consistently. 
- Ashford (38% of Ridgeway): minority passive stake; no attribution to Ridgeway in market shares is warranted on the record, but the Guidelines treat partial ownership/minority interests and cross-ownership could attract FTC interest. Confirm Ashford portfolio holdings in packaging, board rights and information access; unresolved.
- Process: questions to Trident in writing, copy D. Ostrowski; no drafts to the client pending your review.

9. RECOMMENDATIONS (priority order)
1. Commission Brinkerhoff supplement (Market 4 HMT/shares; Market C under 2023 Guidelines; corrections) with scope and dates above. 2. Fix errors: tolling at 60/40 and seller-of-record sensitivity; Market C sums; peripheral-state description; disclose fringe and recompute HHIs; CY and delivered sensitivities. 3. Build the geographic record for 12 states (flow data, bids, diversion) or concede 8-state and argue rebuttal (entry, efficiencies). 4. Demand FTC firm-level data and App. D fringe computations; test identical shares and mixed bases. 5. Reconcile CPS and Ridgeway data to filed totals. 6. Evaluate remedy/divestiture fallback for rigid containers in the Great Lakes region (and food-grade) in case the presumption stands. 7. Confirm Ashford holdings.
